evidence.source: 字源, 李學勤主編, 天津古籍出版社 / 遼寧人民出版社, 2012; direct inspection of supplied full-page scan and enlarged complete paragraph crop; PDF p.145, printed p.133; pixel SHA-256 8bd6a81012882e00aafbf6f3ead6d12a88aec9c0de60f1bfa224588fdbc06529
evidence.field: 邊(边) entry; component roles and four OCR-highlighted occurrences [1618,1619), [1662,1663), [1750,1751), [1809,1810)
evidence.text: The headword is 邊(边). Comparing each highlighted location with repeated forms in the same paragraph, all four spans print 臱, not OCR 昪. The main formation clause assigns movement meaning to 辵 and sound to 臱. Later, the book says the simplified 边 replaces the elaborate 臱 form with 力. A separate proposed oracle-form account describes 自 as 鼻’s original graph and 丙 as a sound element; it is separate from the main 臱 clause. The scan establishes what this book prints, not the ancient sound relationship or whether its 臱 occurrence is historically identical to units named in other accounts.
evidence.title: 字源 — 李學勤主編 (2012)

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, A04196 邊
evidence.field: 字樣說明; 說文释形; Mandarin and cited senses
evidence.text: The entry describes 辶 as the positional form of 辵 and the regular-form right side as 臱, with 自 above and 方 below. It quotes the Shuowen cliff-edge definition and its 辵-plus-sound-unit analysis (the sound glyph is image-rendered in the text view). It gives Mandarin biān and lists frontier, bank/side, edge, limit, directional, and paired 邊…邊… senses. Its examples do not establish first dates or a continuous path among the senses.
evidence.title: A04196 邊 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Chinese Character Database, 邊 record
evidence.field: 《說文》 quotation, 形義通解 and reported bronze inscription uses
evidence.text: The page quotes Shuowen as assigning sound to the specific referent 𦤝 in the small-seal form 𨘢. Separately, it attributes to 張世超 a bronze analysis naming 辵, 自, 丙 and 方: 自 and 丙 are proposed sound elements, 方 contributes ‘beside,’ and ‘beside’ is proposed as the original meaning. It reports a frontier-region use in 大盂鼎 and a place-name 邊柳 in 散氏盤. These are the database’s analysis and reported readings; I did not inspect the artifact images. The page does not establish that 𦤝 is identical with 字源’s printed 臱.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 邊

evidence.field: Historical graph analyses and system-specific reconstructions
evidence.text: The entry presents competing early-form analyses: an oracle-form proposal involving 自 and 丙, and a bronze analysis naming 辵, 自, 丙 and 方 with different proposed sound and meaning roles. It reports a small-seal corruption analysis involving 方. Its Zhengzhang (2003) table gives 邊 *mpeːn and identifies 臱 as a phonetic-series member; this is distinct from the page’s separately displayed Baxter–Sagart value *pˤe[n]. Those systems must not be merged, and the entry does not by itself prove that 臱 is the sound unit in every historical analysis.
evidence.title: 邊 - 维基词典

evidence.text: The entry gives 臱 *men and 邊 *mpeːn in the Zhengzhang (2003) system, and records 臱’s Middle Chinese as mjien. This supplies a same-system comparison for the two named graphs, but does not establish that the graph 𦤝 quoted by Shuowen is identical with 臱 or validate every attributed host analysis.
evidence.title: 臱 - 維基詞典

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, A04196 邊
evidence.text: The dictionary explicitly describes 辶 as the positional form of 辵. This supports origin_form 辵 → form 辶 as a positional/full-form correspondence, not a chronological ancestry claim.
evidence.title: A04196 邊 — 教育部《異體字字典》

Retire from article use pending corrected evidence and fresh authorship/review: X-329808958ada4117679c and X-0cf77caa85d9c41ac6de. Both contain the incorrect 昪 transcription for the book’s main sound unit and simplified-form replacement. Do not cite either beside the corrected scan evidence. Their other claims require separate support if retained.

字源’s printed referent 臱, the Shuowen referent 𦤝, and 自/丙 in separate early analyses must remain distinct unless a source establishes their identity or historical continuity. The inspected sources do not resolve that relationship or settle which early construction is preferred.

CUHK reports a bronze frontier use and proposes ‘beside’ as original meaning, but its artifact readings were not independently checked here. These are attributed source analyses/reports, not independently verified artifact attestations.

The opened Unicode exact-record pages failed; current Unihan kMandarin readings for the entry and named sound candidates were not externally verified in this pass. No historical sound role for 自 or 丙 is independently validated by current Mandarin readings.
No dated continuous semantic sequence was established from proposed ‘beside’ or reported early frontier use to current edge, boundary, side, direction, limit or paired-construction senses.
